newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Vote on Iraqi oil resolution expected on Wednesday.
newsitem.headline: Vote on Iraqi oil resolution expected on Wednesday.

text.p: The Security Council is expected to approve late Wednesday a six-month renewal of its "oil-for-food" deal with Iraq and to say it will favorably consider yet a further extension if it is satisfied Iraq ensures the equitably distribution of humanitarian supplies.
A resolution circulated would renew the arrangement for another 180-day period, beginning 0001 EDT/0401 GMT June 8.

On the basis of reports from Secretary-General Kofi Annan, the council will conduct a "thorough review of all aspects" of the scheme after 90 days, and again prior to the end of the 180 period, accorlding to a copy of the resolution.

The current deal, which expires on June 7, calls for $2 billion worth of oil sales over six months to be used by Baghdad to buy food and medicine for its people, suffering from economic sanctions imposed in August 1990 when Iraqi troops invaded Kuwait.
The resolution before the council also asks Iraq to submit a new plan for distribution of the goods, including a description of supplies to be purchased with the sale of oil.
A senior Clinton administration at a briefing said the United States as well as Britain were concerned about the lack of detail in U.N. reports submitted so far.
He said that monitoring, particularly in the northern Kurdish areas where the United Nations was to have controlled all the distribution of the goods could be strengthened.
He also said the United Nations was also slow in getting enough of its monitors on the ground in Iraq.
